candidates.title: [Bug]: variable declared with type `never` and no initializer is not rejected
[Bug]: XML template accepts a processing instruction with the reserved target `xml`
candidates.body:
### Description
An XML template expression accepts a processing instruction whose target is `xml` in any letter case, including an XML declaration. That text is not well-formed XML `content`, so it should be rejected at compile time.

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    xml x = xml `<?xml version="1.0"?><a/>`; // @error
    io:println(x);
    xml y = xml `<r><?XmL data?></r>`; // @error
    io:println(y);
}
```
Run with `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal`.

**Actual:**
```
<?xml version="1.0"?><a/>
<r><?XmL data?></r>
```

**Expected:** compile errors on both template lines.

**Spec reasoning:**
- §6.6.2 XML template expression: "The result of the previous step is parsed as XML content. More precisely, it is parsed using the production content in the W3C XML Recommendation." The only relaxation is that "each interpolated expression is interpreted as if it were an additional character allowed by the CharData and AttValue productions but no other."
- XML 1.0 [43] `content` does not include `XMLDecl`, so `<?xml ...?>` can only be parsed as a PI. [17] `PITarget ::= Name - (('X' | 'x') ('M' | 'm') ('L' | 'l'))` excludes `xml` in every letter case.
- `xml:fromString` already rejects both strings (`corpus/bal/subset10/10-xml-navigation/lang-xml-errors-v.bal`), so the template path is inconsistent with it. Valid targets such as `xml-stylesheet` and `xmlfoo` must keep working (`subset9/09-template-expr/template-xmlfoo-pi-v.bal`).

### Affected Version(s)
nutcracker `main` @ be382dae3b045fa9708ee3354d10bd019d746c49

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, Go toolchain from `go.mod`

### Related area
Semantics

### Related issue(s) (optional)
#1587 and #1588 are other well-formedness checks missing from XML templates. #1414 asks for `xml:fromString` to accept a leading XML declaration; that is a different path (fromString at document level).

### Suggested label(s) (optional)
Type/Bug

candidates.title: [Bug]: XML template accepts a literal `]]>` in element text
candidates.body: ### Description An XML template expression accepts the sequence `]]>` in character data and escapes it when printing. XML forbids `]]>` in character data, so this template is not well-formed and should be rejected at compile time. ### Steps to Reproduce ```ballerina import ballerina/io; public function main() { xml x = xml `x]]>y`; // @error io:println(x); } ``` Run with `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal`. **Actual:** ``` x]]>y ``` **Expected:** a compile error on the template line. **Spec reasoning:** - §6.6.2 XML template expression: the template text "is parsed using the production content in the W3C XML Recommendation". Interpolations count as extra CharData/AttValue characters "but no other" relaxation is given. - XML 1.0 [14] `CharData ::= [^<&]* - ([^<&]* ']]>' [^<&]*)`. §2.4: the right angle bracket "MUST, for compatibility, be escaped using '>' or a character reference when it appears in the string ']]>' in content, when that string is not marking the end of a CDATA section." - A top-level `xml `]]>`` is accepted the same way and prints `]]>`. ### Affected Version(s) nutcracker `main` @ be382dae3b045fa9708ee3354d10bd019d746c49 ### OS, DB, other environment details and versions Linux, Go toolchain from `go.mod` ### Related area Semantics ### Related issue(s) (optional) #1587 and #1588 (other missing well-formedness checks in XML templates). #1412 (CDATA sections in templates are not supported) is different: this report is about a stray `]]>` in text. ### Suggested label(s) (optional) Type/Bug

candidates.title: [Bug]: calling a resource method that has an unnamed path parameter panics with "too many arguments"
candidates.body:
### Description
A resource method can declare a path parameter with no name, such as `[int]` or `[string...]`. The program compiles and the resource access type-checks, but the call panics at runtime with `too many arguments`.

### Steps to Reproduce
```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

client class C {
    resource function get n/[int]() returns string {
        return "anon";
    }
}

public function main() {
    C c = new;
    string s = c->/n/[3];
    io:println(s); // @output anon
}
```
Run with `go run ./cli/cmd run repro.bal`.

**Actual:**
```
error: too many arguments
        at main(repro.bal:11)
```

**Expected:** prints `anon`.

**Spec reasoning:**
- §5.6.3.5: `resource-path-segment-param := [[annots] type-descriptor [param-name]]` and `resource-path-rest-param := [[annots] type-descriptor ... [param-name]]`, so the name is optional. "A resource-path-segment-param with type descriptor T maps to a member type descriptor T." Only the type determines the path's shape.
- §6.8.1.4: "The list of values supplied for the resource path are used to bind parameters specified in the resource-path before the function is invoked." An unnamed segment has nothing to bind, but the path value is still a valid argument.
- The rest form fails the same way: `resource function get m/[string...]() returns string` called as `c->/m/a/b` panics with `too many arguments`.
- subset10.md lists client resource access actions as supported. Its only restriction (an atomic receiver, and no dispatch when several methods match) does not apply here.

### Affected Version(s)
nutcracker `main` @ be382dae3b045fa9708ee3354d10bd019d746c49

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions
Linux, Go toolchain from `go.mod`

### Related area
Interpreter

### Related issue(s) (optional)
None found.

### Suggested label(s) (optional)
Type/Bug

notes:
Spec fetched from https://ballerina.io/spec/lang/master/ (ok). Interpreter built from upstream main @ be382dae3b045fa9708ee3354d10bd019d746c49.
Hit the 5-confirmed-candidate limit after about 35 minutes. Unfinished work is listed below.

Candidates dropped as duplicates of open issues: #1044, #1753, #1487, #1047, #1149, #1046, #1249, #163, #1223, #1215, #1147, #1050, #1538, #1511, #1076, #1166 and #1351.
Candidate dropped as deliberate project behaviour: `never _ = expr;` is accepted (corpus call-arg-never-p.bal).

Unverified leads that were not deduplicated or validated (stopped at the limit). Both 1 and 2 are compiler crashes:
1. `function init() returns error? => ();` crashes the compiler: Go panic "interface conversion: ast.FunctionBodyNode is *ast.BLangExprFunctionBody, not *ast.BLangBlockFunctionBody" in projects.runPerModule (package_compilation.go:252).
2. `type Nested int|Nested[][];` gives "fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: type env not ready when draining deferred emptiness checks". Adding `type Other [int, Other...];` gives a nil-pointer panic in semtypes.listFormulaIsEmpty.
3. Unsound missing-return check: `function v() {} function h() returns int { v(); }` compiles, and h() returns nil, so `h() + 1` fails at runtime with "unsupported type combination: <nil> + int64". Any function body ending in a call statement passes the missing-return check (cfg_analyzer.go terminalBlockHasReturnOrPanic).
4. A class including an intersection of distinct object types (`*DAB` where `type DAB DA & DB;`) is rejected; probably covered by #1287.
5. Possible comments: #1511 does not cover toBalString of an object with a toString method (`[object P<x>,\"q\"]` expected). #1166 does not cover default params being evaluated between explicit named args.
